findings.message: the connector manifest this run was judged by is not the one this build pins: the pin is e55b0dc45fd6dc758db386238ecdf4633be5868929144302e738811fa56ea1e1, and the file `trace.toml` named hashes to 025e490413b51fee20b283f101d6777cf98e62cdeec3afe3e1c42fc5f299b9c5. the manifest supplies the human rule, the exclusion catalogue and the tool classes, so a participant free to write it is free to write the rule that excludes their own steering messages — which V2 then has nothing to fail

findings.message: the connector directory this run was captured with is not one this build ships: the receipt claims 8a439f00fdd9489fe7ea165b848f0540cf537afd799fbb861d9820adbf4c9db4 for `claude-code-cli`, and no directory pin of this build's has that digest. the daemon renders the hook bodies under `files/` into the workspace, records their rendered digests as the config it will guard, and then guards them — so an edited template is not a file that slipped past a check, it is the file every later check agrees with. The manifest beside it can be pinned and unchanged while this is true

evidence.note: key source: pinned, and the key is the M1 placeholder

findings.message: the key that verified this trace's server signatures is the M1 placeholder anchor, whose private seed is published in this repository so the fixtures can sign with it. Anybody can mint a receipt or an acknowledgement under it, so a `key_source` of `pinned` says only that the signature matched a key everyone holds. Replacing the placeholder with the real organiser key is the release gate before any entry is judged
